commit.message:
Add tone and precision rules to the skill

Rename the first group to word choice and tone, and move the
hyphenated-adjectives rule into it. Add four rules: keep the writing
boring and descriptive with no catchy phrases, never put three or more
clauses in one sentence, prefer long explanatory sentences over short
punchy ones, and make every claim precise and unambiguous. Move the
inanimate-subject rule into patterns to avoid and drop the old lists
rule that the clause-count rule replaces.

commit.message:
Add rule 25: be precise and unambiguous

Every claim says exactly what changes, who does what, or by what
mechanism. No evocative abstractions like "improvement stops being
guesswork" where a concrete statement exists.

commit.message:
Add rule 24: prefer long, explanatory sentences over short, punchy ones

The user writes the way people explain things out loud, in longer
sentences with commas and several clauses. Plain means explanatory,
not terse.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Fable 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Add rule 23: do not open with a count of things

Never start a sentence, paragraph, or topic sentence by announcing how
many points are coming ("Two cautions.", "Three things to keep in
mind:"). State the first point directly, or use a bullet list when the
count is genuinely useful.

commit.message:
Restructure rules into four groups with inline examples

Group the rules into word choice, sentences and paragraphs, punctuation and
formatting, and patterns to avoid. Put a before and after under each rule
instead of a separate examples section. Add rules for paragraph structure
(topic sentence then support), and reword the demonstrative rule to ban vague
demonstratives and vague summary nouns like "the result", and to forbid
starting a paragraph with a sentence that contains a demonstrative. Add "reach
for" to the overused words and "worth" stays in the puffery list. Fix two
example pairs whose before and after described different things.

Add "worth" to the empty-emphasis blacklist (rule 10)

Catches puffery like "it's worth noting" / "worth considering", alongside
"matters" and "carries weight".

Allow compound sentences and bold list headers

Rule 2: stop splitting every compound sentence into two. Join
related ideas with "and", "because", "so" when they belong
together. Only split when the ideas are unrelated.

Rule 13: bold is fine as a structural header on list items
where the bold text names the thing and the rest explains it.

with an execCommand fallback for older browsers and unfocused pages.

commit.message:
Add rules 14-15: stacked rhetorical questions and dramatic pivots

Both are common AI writing patterns. Stacked rhetorical questions
sound practiced; the dramatic pivot ("X is opaque. Y, but Y is
only one symptom") is a recognizable setup-then-reveal move.

Group most new signs into existing rules (buzzwords and synonym-swapping into

tail into rule 6, puffery into rule 10). Add rule 12 (no vague attribution) and
rule 13 (plain formatting). Add worked examples 8 to 12. Reword the two-jobs
line in rule 2.
